title: Component contract
description: The shape every component's metadata must satisfy. Brand-agnostic: it names no component, no token, no product and no value. Half of a contract is derived from the component's source and half is authored by a person in metadata/authored/<component>.json; which half is which is recorded on each property as "x-origin".

status.description: Where the component sits in its lifecycle.

source.description: Repository-relative path to the file this contract's props were read from.

propsType.description: The name of the type the props were read from.

extends.description: Types the props declaration inherits from. Inherited members are deliberately not enumerated as props: this contract describes what the component decided, not what the platform already provides.

purpose.description: What the component is for, in one or two sentences.

responsibilities.description: What the component owns, and by omission what it does not.

do_not_use_when.description: Boundaries, not instructions. Each entry is a situation this component is the wrong answer to, and what the right answer is instead.

alternatives.description: What to reach for instead, at the boundaries above. An entry naming a component in this system is checked against the other contracts.

constraints.description: What a consumer may not customise, and why.

guarantees.description: What the component guarantees without the consumer doing anything.

consumer_must.description: What the component cannot guarantee on the consumer's behalf.

stylesheet.description: Repository-relative path to the stylesheet beside the component, when there is one. The token list below is read from it.

tokens.description: Tokens this component consumes, by name. Read from the stylesheet's custom property references rather than listed by hand: names only, and a contract that restated what a token resolves to would be a second source for that value.

tokens_absent.description: Custom properties the stylesheet names deliberately and the token set does not define — a token the component asked for and the system has not decided. Declared, tracked, reported, ungated; an undeclared one fails generation.

props.description: Every prop the component's own props type declares. Derived from the source; the authored half may annotate a prop but may not name, type or default one.

figma.description: The Figma-to-code mapping. Property names are authored — they are what the library actually calls things — and the list of props they map to is derived, so a prop cannot quietly stop having a Figma side.

unmapped.description: Props with no Figma property, and why not.

aiHints.description: The component's identity for an agent. Keywords are what let one find this component instead of scaffolding a duplicate.

not_a.description: What this component is repeatedly mistaken for.

deprecation.description: How this component would be withdrawn. Written before it is needed, because the version written afterwards is a negotiation.

generated.description: Where this file came from. It is build output: edit the source or the authored half, then regenerate.

use.description: What to use instead. When it is a component in this system, spell it exactly as that component's contract names it.

in_system.description: True when `use` names a component this system publishes. Checked against the other contracts.

values.description: The members of a closed string union, when the type is one.

description.description: The prop's JSDoc in the source. Authored in the component, derived into here: a description a person could edit in this file would be a second copy of a sentence that already exists.

notes.description: The rest of the prop's JSDoc prose, one entry per paragraph. Derived like the summary above it, and kept as paragraphs because a twenty-line explanation collapsed into one string is faithful and unreadable.

guidance.description: What a person knows about the prop that its type does not say.

figmaProperty.description: The Figma property this prop mirrors, or null when it has none.
